sources.entry: Haystack Editor - Code editor with a canvas UI for better code understanding. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/haystackeditor/haystack-editor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Haystack Editor is a source-available code editor from Haystack Software that pairs standard code editing with a canvas-style UI intended to help users understand code at a glance.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Haystack Editor as a code editor with a canvas UI, offering code editing, navigation, and understanding support, plus lightweight debugging, an extensibility model, and integration with existing tools. The repository is where Haystack Software develops the product and publishes its roadmap, and it accepts bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests. The editor ships as a distribution of this repo with specific customizations under a terms of service. A bundled extensions folder includes grammars and snippets for many languages, and language-features extensions add completion and Go to Definition. The README lists feature sections for Canvas Workspaces, Explorer View, Keyboard Navigation, and Generate Function, but their content is not included in the text. Downloads are said to be available for Windows, macOS, and Linux from the company website.
use_cases: Reading and navigating an unfamiliar codebase visually
Editing code with a canvas-style workspace
Contributing to or building an open-source code editor
Reporting bugs or requesting features for Haystack Editor
how_to_run: Download the editor for Windows, macOS, or Linux from Haystack's website (per the README)
To build and run from source, see the How to Contribute document referenced in the README
stack: VS Code-style extension system (bundled extensions folder)
notable: Canvas UI for viewing and understanding code at a glance
Bundled language grammars, snippets, and language-features extensions
Separate debug adapter repositories for node and mono
Publicly published roadmap alongside the source
caveats: Licensed under PolyForm Strict, which is source-available rather than an open-source license
Distributed builds are governed by a terms of service and specific customizations
README does not describe platform specifics beyond the three desktop OSes named
